jewelry.name: necklace
jewelry.title: necklace
jewelry.reason: A squash-blossom style necklace made of steel, attributed to a Laguna Pueblo maker; squash-blossom necklaces are a well-known Southwest Puebloan/Navajo jewelry form, plausible for Laguna.

jewelry.name: bracelet
jewelry.title: bracelet
jewelry.reason: A metal cuff bracelet with silver inlay bands and a zig-zag mountain motif, attributed by the museum to a Laguna Pueblo silversmith—a plausible form of Southwest Pueblo silverwork.

ceramic.name: vessel, pot,
ceramic.title: vessel, pot,
ceramic.reason: Classic Laguna Pueblo polychrome storage jar with black-and-red geometric and feather motifs on white slip, a well-documented traditional pottery type made by this people.

ceramic.name: kärl, kruka, vessel
ceramic.title: kärl, kruka, vessel
ceramic.reason: A classic wedding-vase style small ceramic jar with twin spouts joined by a handle, painted with black and red geometric/floral designs on white slip — characteristic of Laguna Pueblo pottery traditions.

ceramic.name: kärl, Lerkärl
ceramic.title: kärl, Lerkärl
ceramic.reason: A small handmade earthenware jar with broken-off handle, cream slip and brown-black geometric triangle/eye design, consistent with traditional Pueblo pottery; museum records it as from Laguna Pueblo, New Mexico.

ceramic.name: skål, Lerskål, kärl
ceramic.title: skål, Lerskål, kärl
ceramic.reason: A cream-slipped earthenware bowl with dark brown triangular/geometric painted band, explicitly documented as from Laguna Pueblo, New Mexico, consistent with historic Laguna pottery traditions.

photo.name: by, landskap, fotografi, photograph
photo.title: by, landskap, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: The photograph shows the Pueblo of Laguna, New Mexico, with its adobe buildings on the hill above the San José River — a documentary view of the village the Laguna people built and live in.

photo.name: Žena kojící dítě
photo.title: Žena kojící dítě
photo.reason: The picture is a documentary photograph of a woman in traditional dress holding an infant on a cradleboard in her lap, with handwritten caption noting "Laguna Pueblo, New Mexico" — this is ethnographic documentation of Laguna Pueblo life, not a sculpture.
